headline: High risk of shared-workspace write conflicts and cascading automation errors; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and pass stdin/stdout, while Transformers can run browsers and process text; if outputs are bridged through shared files or copied prompts, injected instructions could be re-ingested. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is an inferred, low-blast-radius pathway.
conditions: IF agent_a writes model-facing text into a shared file that agent_b later parses as instructions
IF agent_b consumes raw text from agent_a via stdin/stdout or copied artifacts without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable automatic parsing of generated text as instructions
Add a provenance header to all inter-agent files
Review any shared file handoff before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and Transformers can read/write files and use broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive data can flow from Kestra into Transformers' inference or Hub/API traffic. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same directory or artifact store
IF Kestra places logs, inputs, or database data into files that Transformers reads
IF Transformers sends those files to a remote backend or Hub endpoint
mitigations: Use separate storage roots for each agent
Restrict Transformers to local-only execution
Redact logs and artifacts before handoff
Rotate or isolate credentials from shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, read_filesystem, write_filesystem, and broad network egress. Kestra also requests root and docker.sock, while Transformers can install packages and run browsers. On a shared directory or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and package/runtime changes can corrupt state or overwrite each other's outputs.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF either agent mutates shared runtime dependencies or model files
IF concurrent instances operate without locking on shared mutable resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run each agent in its own container
Pin and freeze dependencies before execution
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra produces workflow definitions, logs, variables, artifacts, and notifications; Transformers can consume text and generate downstream outputs. If Transformers treats Kestra output as authoritative, a bad workflow artifact or log-derived instruction can cascade into incorrect documents, browser actions, or model-serving behavior. The interaction is plausible and dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Transformers consumes Kestra-generated artifacts or logs without verification
IF Kestra notifications or workflow text are used as prompts or task specs
IF downstream actions are triggered from unvalidated model output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on generated text
Require schema validation on Kestra outputs
Mark machine-generated artifacts as untrusted
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra explicitly touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Transformers handles text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data. With no residency, retention, or certification details in either profile, a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is routed through the pair. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or secrets is routed through both agents
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two deployments
IF one agent logs or stores data longer than the other
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through the pair
Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Document retention and deletion settings
Verify residency and DPA coverage
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both deployments
